subject.title: [Feishu] "This reply completed without visible content" fallback incorrectly triggered for long/markdown-heavy replies (regression from #87896)

question: Is the session-level report enough to promote a fix investigation now, or should maintainers require live Feishu or trajectory proof showing where the long markdown final is lost before coding?
rationale: Current source proves the fallback fires after zero-final accounting, but not why a generated long markdown final reaches that state; choosing the wrong fix layer could suppress a valid empty-turn warning or add another silent-drop path.

options.title: Require live or trajectory proof first
options.body: Ask for a redacted Feishu transcript/log or run a live reproduction that captures assistant final extraction, delivery attempts, failed counts, and fallback trigger before promoting a repair.

options.title: Promote guarded source investigation
options.body: Allow a repair worker only if it first creates a focused failing harness for the long-markdown zero-final path and avoids broad fallback-policy changes.

recommendation.title: Require live or trajectory proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for a redacted Feishu transcript/log or run a live reproduction that captures assistant final extraction, delivery attempts, failed counts, and fallback trigger before promoting a repair.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged and authored most follow-up commits in the Feishu fallback repair line, so he is the best evidenced owner for the proof-sufficiency call.
